body.html:
Context

Why Fake Bank exists

Payment integrations need a provider on the other side of the transaction. Fake Bank supplies that boundary in a controlled local environment: a payment API, a buyer-facing checkout and events sent back to the merchant.

Simulated payments

Exercise payment flows without moving real money.

Explicit scenarios

Select success, failure and timing behavior.

Independent by design

Connect a merchant application through the provider contract.

Problem

What needs to be solved

A successful checkout is only part of an integration. Delayed results, declined payments, missing events and duplicate deliveries all affect merchant state. A controlled simulator makes these paths repeatable during development.

  • Payment lifecycle transitions
  • Hosted checkout and card simulation
  • Delayed and duplicate webhook scenarios
  • Timeout and provider-error behavior
  • A local, inspectable provider boundary

Architecture

System design

The merchant owns its orders and business logic. Fake Bank owns simulated provider payments, checkout state, scenario execution and webhook delivery attempts. PostgreSQL stores provider records and events.

Read the architecture →

Implementation

Key components

A TypeScript API built with Fastify serves the payment contract. React provides hosted checkout. Named scenarios control outcomes; PostgreSQL records payments and webhook attempts. Docker Compose supports local execution.

API contract →Local setup →

Verification

Testing and validation

The repository contains automated checks for payment routes, lifecycle behavior, scenario outcomes and webhook delivery. These checks define expected behavior; they do not establish production readiness.

Runtime acceptance has not been rerun for this page. Published verification results remain pending.

Repository evidence Source review

  • Payment creation and input validation
  • Checkout confirmation and lifecycle transitions
  • Scenario and webhook behavior
  • OpenAPI and migration validation scripts
  • Reference merchant integration

Test definitions present · Runtime results pending

Status

Current status

Fake Bank is available as an open-source simulator for local development and integration work. The repository includes setup instructions, API documentation and a reference merchant. Public hosted-demo availability has not been verified.

Independent provider simulator
